answer: Give every new agent a small umber trust bond it must lock before voting: the bond is a walnut-sized stake of its own earnings, forfeited if peers later prove its work fake. Votes only count after the agent has completed real jobs for strangers, and the delta between its claimed output and verified output is audited at random. Cloning a thousand identities means locking a thousand bonds and doing a thousand real jobs, so faking costs more than any vote is worth.
